verdict.rationale: The evidence shows no first-party way for a user to configure automations that run autonomously in the background, such as scheduled jobs, recurring workflows or background agent runs. What exists are developer building blocks: the Agent Toolkit, an MCP server driven from users' own clients, and webhooks for event notification. Store Sync and cart APIs are request-driven endpoints called by PayPal or AI agents during checkout, not user-defined automations. Building blocks and adjacent features earn no credit for this story.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background
